endorsements.quote: This report presents a standardized evaluation framework (Appendix) that will enable authors to demonstrate the validity of AI methods used in their work, thereby improving transparency enhancing robustness, and accelerating growth in the AI/IR field.
There is also a section for the authors to explain the likely cause of each potential bias that may affect the AI models developed in their study (if applicable).
Researchers are also required to provide information about bias mitigation techniques, consent processes, regulatory oversight, and data privacy protections.

unlisted_practices: Authors of AI research should report pre-training data sources and methods, and explain why pre-trained models were not used.
Authors should explain why testing was limited when test sets come from a single-origin dataset also used for training and validation.
Authors should report the involvement of clinicians in data annotation and in the interpretation of explainability outputs.
Authors should report the AI-readiness of publicly released datasets, including data use agreements or usage guidelines addressing use with LLM APIs.
Authors should report code, model weights, and data availability for reproducibility.
Authors should report an AI model's deployment level, clinical workflow disruption, and planned next steps toward clinical use.

screen.reason: This report presents reporting standards and an evaluation checklist (iCARE) for artificial intelligence research evaluation and clinical pipeline governance in interventional radiology.
